To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new technique to derive spatial distributions of the average energy of the precipitated auroral electrons from simultaneous images of the aurora in three spectral bands.
the ratio of the FUV SI13 and WIC signals can be used as a proxy of the characteristic energy and flux of auroral electron precipitation.
the FUV imager can detect auroral precipitation events with spatial scale as small as ∼200 km and can provide information on the average electron energy distribution in the auroral zone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the auroral precipitation and its time and spatial dynamics as deduced from IMAGE FUV images.
the development of a method to derive the average energy of auroral electron precipitation from simultaneous FUV images in the WIC and the SI13 channels.
the development of new methods for analyzing auroral images in order to characterize the electron precipitation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the FUV ratio method provides a useful tool for investigating the spatial and temporal evolution of electron precipitation in the auroral zone, but that the interpretation of the results is limited to a description of the precipitation characteristics.
the ratio method provides a good estimation of the average energy of the electron precipitation and of its spatial and temporal distribution.

the ratio method is useful in determining the average energy of the precipitated electrons and their energy fluxes.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the FUV ratio method provides a unique tool to study the spatial and time evolution of the electron precipitation during substorm events, with a ∼2 min temporal resolution and a 200 km spatial resolution.
the ratio method is able to provide information on the spatial and temporal variations of the average energy of precipitating electrons.
